nodes.title: Free the VRAM - the rest is mesh work
2. Back view - you see the back
Settings for your card
widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

SETTINGS FOR YOUR GRAPHICS CARD

 Use the views you have

The model does not need all four. Switch off any view you do not have on the 5. Which views do you have? node and it works from the rest. Any combination runs, down to a single picture.

You do not even have to keep the Front one. With Front off, the first view still switched on becomes the front, and the model is posed to face that way instead - so a back-only run gives you a model whose back is facing forward. Everything still lines up, you just have to turn the result round. Leaving Front on saves you that.

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own robot pictures, same seed. Thickness is how deep the model came out compared with the four-view one.

Views switched onWhat you getThickness
All fourThe robot as drawn100%
Front + Back + LeftLooks the same as all four, front and back99%
Front + LeftFront and side right, a second visor made up on the back of the head99%
Front + BackFront and back right, but thinner92%
Front onlyThe front right, the chest button copied onto the back103%

Three views came out looking the same as all four. Leave the Back out and the model has to invent the back: from front and left it put a second visor on the back of the head.

If you only have two, pick them by what matters on your subject. Front and a side get the depth right but guess the back. Front and back get the back right, but tell the model nothing about how deep the subject is, and the robot came out 8% too thin.

Switching views off saves little time. Reading the views takes about 7 seconds each, and a shape guessed from fewer views can come out bigger and take longer to rebuild and bake. Use the switches for accuracy, not for speed.

 The four numbers that decide the speed

Everything else in the workflow can stay as it is. Each row says which node to look for.

SettingNode on the canvasFasterThis workflowFaster saves
Upsample resolutionUpsample the shape10241024already the lowest
Texture size7. Texture size20484096about 16 s
Rebuild resolutionRebuild the mesh cleanly7681024about 14 s
TrianglesReduce to N triangles200,000700,000about 9 s

Each saving was measured on its own, changing that one setting and running again. The upsample is already at its lowest here. Raising it to 1536 costs about 19 seconds and keeps small details more often, but it leaves small flat facets on round surfaces that no rebuild setting removes. Do not go above 1536: the node allows 2048, but in testing it made the mesh messier, with about twice as many broken edges and three times as many loose bits, and its details were no closer to the pictures.

Rebuild 1024 with smoothing 6 is the quality setting. In testing it kept the surface closest to what the model made, with crisper edges than smoothing 20, while a rebuild at 1536 tore holes in the model. The rebuilt mesh is also what the normal map and the ambient occlusion are baked from.

 Measured run time

On a 24 GB RTX 4090, with all four views on, this workflow finished in about 2 minutes 33 seconds. Reading the four views takes about 30 seconds, the mesh clean-up about 20, and the baking about 70, the ambient occlusion bake alone 42; the rest is the four passes that build the shape and the colours. The very first run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk.

Change a setting near the end and Run again, and only the steps after it run again. Here that still includes the baking, so a new triangle count or texture size took about a minute and a half.

The graphics card peaked at about 11 GB. That is what ComfyUI chose to use on a 24 GB card, not what the workflow needs.

The Stage 1 result viewer fills in early with a rough blob, which tells you the run is alive. There are two results. The FAST RESULT shows the colours painted on the mesh points. The FULL RESULT has real texture maps, and that is the one written to output/3d. Both arrive at the end of the run, after the baking.

 What makes a good set of pictures

  • Same subject, same pose, same lighting in every picture.
  • The same distance every time, so the subject is the same size in each one.
  • A plain background. The workflow cuts it out anyway, but a busy one confuses the cut-out.
  • Renders from a turnaround work best. Photographs work too, as long as you move a quarter turn around the subject each time.

 Left and right are the part people get wrong

The names are about where the camera is standing, not which way the subject is turned. Stand on someone's left and look at them, and their face points off to the left of your picture.

SlotWhat the picture should show
frontThe subject looks at you
leftThe subject looks to the LEFT edge of the frame
backYou see its back
rightThe subject looks to the RIGHT edge of the frame

Get these the wrong way round and the shape still builds, because most subjects are close to symmetrical, but anything on one side only ends up on the wrong side.

 Why Free VRAM is in the workflow

The Free VRAM node sits after the colours are worked out, the last step that needs the big model. It hands the card's memory back before the colours are baked into the texture maps, which also runs on the graphics card.

nodes.title: What each node does
widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the other note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Pixal3D Multi-View) - The model that turns the pictures into a 3D shape.
  • Load CLIP Vision (DINOv3) - Reads the pictures so the model understands what it is looking at.
  • Load VAE (shape) - Turns the model's output into geometry.
  • Load VAE (texture) - Turns the model's output into colours.
  • Cut out the background - Cuts the subject away from its background. One per view, all using the same file.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Front view - looks at you - The subject facing the camera.
  • 2. Back view - you see the back - The subject with its back to the camera.
  • 3. Left view - looks LEFT - Taken from the subject's left. In the picture it faces the left edge.
  • 4. Right view - looks RIGHT - Taken from the subject's right. In the picture it faces the right edge.
  • 5. Which views do you have? - Four switches: Front, Back, Left, Right. Click one to turn that view off and the model works from whatever is left. A switched-off view is skipped entirely, so it costs you nothing. Any combination runs, even a single picture, and you do not have to keep the front one.
  • 6. Seed (drives all four samplers) - Same seed, nearly the same result. Change it for a different attempt.
  • 7. Texture size (lower = faster) - Size of the baked texture maps.

 Getting the pictures ready

Grey. Runs by itself, no numbers to type.

  • Centre and crop to 1024 x 1024 - Puts each subject in the middle at the size the model expects. One per view.
  • Front / Back / Left / Right - what the model sees - The cut-out view, and also what feeds the model. Check these before a long run: a bad cut-out here is the usual reason a result comes out wrong.
  • Read the views - Hands the switched-on views to the model, telling it which angle each was taken from.

 Stage 1

Teal. A rough blob, so you can see it is working.

  • Empty 3D latent - The empty space the shape gets built into.
  • Stage 1 - rough voxel blob - First pass. Blocks out roughly where the object is.
  • Decode the blob - Turns that first pass into something viewable.
  • Voxel to Mesh - Converts the blocks into a mesh.
  • Stage 1 result - the rough blob - What the first pass produced. Lumpy is correct here.

 Stage 2

Purple. The real shape appears.

  • Shape stage - Sets up the pass that finds the real shape.
  • Stage 2 - the real shape - Second pass. The actual form appears.

 Stage 3

Red. The shape is refined and upscaled.

  • Upsample the shape to 1024 - How finely the shape is built. 1536 keeps small details more often, but leaves flat facets on round surfaces and takes longer.
  • Stage 3 - refine the shape - Third pass. Cleans up and adds detail.
  • Decode the mesh - Turns the refined result into a mesh.

 Stage 4

Green. The colours are worked out.

  • Texture stage - Sets up the pass that works out the colours.
  • Stage 4 - the colours - Fourth pass. Colour per point on the surface.
  • Decode the colours - Turns that pass into usable colour data.

 After the stages

Amber. Mesh tidy-up, texture baking and saving.

  • Free the VRAM - the rest is mesh work - Hands the graphics card's memory back once the colours are worked out, before the colour bake.
  • Mesh info (polygon count) - Reports how many points and faces the mesh has.
  • Rebuild the mesh cleanly - Rebuilds the surface as an even grid of triangles. The model's own mesh is messy in places, and most 3D programs want a tidy one.
  • Reduce to 700k triangles - Cuts the triangle count down to something usable.
  • Smooth the normals - Smooths the shading so the surface does not look faceted.
  • Paint the mesh with the colours - Puts the colours onto the mesh points.
  • FAST RESULT - vertex colours - Turn it with the mouse. Colour on the points, no texture files.
  • UV unwrap - Flattens the mesh so textures can be painted onto it.
  • Bake colour / roughness / metallic - Renders three texture maps from the colours the model worked out.
  • Bake the normal map - Renders a map that fakes small surface detail.
  • Bake ambient occlusion - Renders the soft shadows in the crevices.
  • Base Color - The colour map, for checking.
  • Metallic - The metal map, for checking.
  • Roughness - The roughness map, for checking.
  • Normal - The normal map, for checking.
  • Ambient Occlusion - The shadow map, for checking.
  • Apply all the maps - Attaches every baked map to the mesh.
  • FULL RESULT - saved to output/3d - The finished model with its texture maps, written to output/3d as a .glb.

 Left alone on purpose

No colour means you never need to change it.

  • Pipeline default - leave alone - Part of how the model runs. Nothing to change.

{"version":1,"content":"

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 Load Diffusion Model

Download pixal3d_multiview_int8_convrot.safetensors~5.2 GB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/3D

Create the 3D folder if it does not exist.

This is the multi-view Pixal3D model. It is a different file from the single-picture one, and it is the only one that can read four views at once.

 Load CLIP Vision

Download dino_v3_L_naf_fp32.safetensors~1.1 GB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/clip_vision

 Load VAE (two files)

Download trellis_2_shape_vae_bf16.safetensors~1.0 GB 

Download trellis_2_texture_vae_bf16.safetensors~0.9 GB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

 Remove Background Pixaroma

Download birefnet.safetensors~424 MB 

Place in: ComfyUI/models/background_removal

One file. The four Cut out the background nodes all use it, and it is only loaded once.

 After placing the files, restart ComfyUI or refresh model lists using the R shortcut.

 Nodes Installed from Manager

  • Pixaroma

 Resources

Join Discord  Pixaroma YouTube Channel
